messages:
Maya: Quick copy check for the 'quota exceeded' empty state in the console. Current header: 'Quota reached' and body 'You have used all of your tokens.' Sounds abrupt. Any better phrasing?

Eli: We should lead with the user outcome and next step. Maybe 'Hit your quota' is friendlier? Also suggest hint about when quota resets or how to increase it.

Rhea: Draft: Header 'Quota reached' Body 'You've used your plan's token allowance. Upgrade or wait until your quota resets at the start of your billing period.' CTA primary 'Upgrade plan' secondary 'Billing details'

Maya: I like explicitness but keep the body scannable. Maybe shorten: 'You've used your plan's token allowance. Upgrade to continue or check billing details.'

DesignBot: Accessibility note: avoid embedding links in long sentences; keep separate CTAs. Also avoid jargon like 'tokens' for non-technical users; use 'usage' or 'quota' instead. Localization: shorter sentences help translate cost.

Eli: New proposed strings for Figma/components: Header: "Quota reached" Body: "You've used your plan's allowance. Upgrade to continue or view billing details." Primary CTA: "Upgrade plan" Secondary CTA: "View billing" Tooltip for CTA: "Upgrade your plan"

Rhea: Tiny tone nit: 'Upgrade plan' can feel pushy. Consider 'Upgrade' alone in the button, with aria-label 'Upgrade plan' for clarity. But I think explicit label is fine in this product context.

Maya: Good call about 'tokens' -> 'allowance'. I'll update the empty-state component and add aria-describedby linking the body to the CTAs. Will open a PR with the strings and include localization flag for product.

Eli: Thanks! Tagging @product for billing copy review.
